title: Romans and Galatians: justification from works = by law; from faith = without works
source_text: XXXVI. Hanc esse Apostoli mentem, agnoscet facile quisquis attente considerabit quae Paulus hac de re disserit in Epist. ad Rom. & Epist. ad Galatas. Nam Paulo justificari ex operibus simpliciter, justificari ex operibus legis, & justificari per legem, idem sunt. Sicut pro eodem habet justificari ex fide, & justificari sine operibus. Justitia autem legis, secundum Pauli doctrinam, in eo consistit ut quis accurate faciat omnia quae lege jubentur, quemadmodum justus ex fide est ille qui viva fide credit in Christum, quoniam tali sua fides ad justitiam imputatur. Nam opponit sedulo legem, quae fidem non postulat, sed perfectam obedientiam, & dicit, Qui fecerit ea homo, vivet in eis. Item, Execrabilis quisquis non manserit in omnibus quae scripta sunt in libro legis, ut faciat ea. Verbo fidei sive Evangelio, quod justitiam & salutem gratuito offert, utpote cujus summa haec sit, Si professus fueris ore tuo Dominum Jesum, & credideris in corde tuo quod Deus eum suscitavit ex mortuis, servaberis, Rom. 10. & Gal. 5.
pass_a_gloss: Anyone who carefully considers what Paul discusses on this matter in Romans and Galatians will easily acknowledge that this is the Apostle's mind. For for Paul to be justified from works simply, to be justified from works of the law, and to be justified through the law are the same. Just as he holds as the same to be justified from faith and to be justified without works. But the righteousness of the law, according to Paul's teaching, consists in accurately doing all that the law commands, just as the one righteous from faith is the one who believes in Christ with living faith, because to such his faith is imputed for righteousness. For he carefully opposes the law, which does not require faith but perfect obedience, and says: The person who does them shall live by them. Likewise: Accursed is whoever does not continue in all that is written in the book of the law, to do them. To the word of faith or Gospel, which freely offers righteousness and salvation, whose sum is this: If you confess with your mouth the Lord Jesus and believe in your heart that God raised him from the dead, you will be saved (Rom 10; Gal 5).
pass_b_english: For Paul, justification from works = by law; from faith = without works.
Law demands perfect doing; gospel sum is confess-and-believe (Rom 10).

choices.why: Works / works of law / by law equate for Paul.
